title: indigo_mount_driver: refuse a sync within 5 degrees of the celestial pole instead of warning, it sends later GoTos to the other side of the pier (reported for indigo_mount_synscan 3.0.0.22)
description:
Origin: a user who upgraded to 3.0-11 reported that the SynScan driver moves the mount in the opposite direction on GoTo; it was correct before 3.0.0.22.

Cause, established by running the same sequence on an AZ-GTi with drivers 3.0.0.20, 3.0.0.21 and 3.0.0.22 and reading the axis counters straight from the motor controller (see the notes): GoTos without an alignment point end at the same axis positions in all three versions (3.0.0.22 differs by the intended precession only). After a sync in the home position (RA = LST - 6 h, Dec 90) 3.0.0.20 and 3.0.0.21 go where they went without it, 3.0.0.22 ends on the other side of the pier (target HA +2.5 h: RA axis +313314 instead of -302393 steps) and still publishes the target coordinates. Since 3.0.0.22 the raw coordinates are J2000, so at the pole of the date the raw right ascension no longer equals LST - hour angle and the alignment point of the framework model records a right ascension offset of hours. Near the pole no right ascension offset can be measured in any frame.

Owner decision (2026-11-18, supersedes the earlier ones in the notes): change the pole sync warning of indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c (commit d7f5c4e30, not released yet) into a refusal with an error. The SynScan driver itself is not changed; its coordinate frames stay as in 3.0.0.22.

Change:
- indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c, sync branch of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES in the framework alignment modes: when the requested declination or the raw declination is more than 85 degrees from the equator, the request is refused: MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES is published in ALERT with a message, no alignment point is added and the requested values are not adopted, the property keeps the real pointing. The warning message on the BUSY property is removed. A request without the declination item is judged by the declination the property holds.
- Tests: unit case of the warning turned into the refusal (indigo_test/unit/test_mount_alignment_load.c); SynScan simulator suite: new case for the refused home sync in both hemispheres followed by an accurate GoTo, the existing sync case leaves the pole first; mount simulator suite: the case that synced at the pole leaves it first; SynScan hardware suite: new case for the refused home sync followed by an accurate GoTo.
- Recorded runs: tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan (simulator) and --hw (AZ-GTi on the network, non-interactive, no hot-plug).

Known limitation: alignment points with an offset of hours that a pole sync already saved under 3.0.0.22 stay in the user's configuration until deleted with MOUNT_ALIGNMENT_DELETE_POINTS. Baseline: mount_abort_allows_fresh_goto of the mount simulator suite fails on master as well (test_mount_simulator.c, target RA after an alignment mode change) and is not part of this ticket.

outcome.summary:
Verdict: changes (one must-fix in the new simulator test; the library change itself is correct).

MUST-FIX
1. indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c:3338 - SERIAL_CHECK_TRUE(fabs(synscan_wrap_hours(refused_ra - sync_values[0])) > 1) depends on the sidereal time. In the home position the reported RA is fixed (23.9885 h north / 11.9885 h south, the J2000 place of the pole of date, see the case printout), while the requested RA is LST - 6 h (north) / LST + 6 h (south). Whenever LST is between about 4.99 h and 6.99 h the two are within 1 h in both hemispheres and the case fails although the driver behaves correctly: roughly 2 sidereal hours per day, so the recorded suite is time-of-day flaky. Fix: assert the refusal carried the real pointing instead, e.g. SERIAL_CHECK_TRUE(fabs(synscan_wrap_hours(refused_ra - home_ra)) < 0.01); the declination checks at 3335-3336 already prove the requested values were not adopted. Re-run the case (and the recorded run if the owner wants the record on the final tree).

LIMITATIONS (for the owner, not blocking)
- indigo_drivers/agent_mount/indigo_agent_mount.c:433-495 with indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver:983-985: the refusal ALERT is transient on SynScan, its next poll republishes MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES OK. A sync is never BUSY, so Mount Agent waits its full 3 s BUSY window, then sees OK and only compares the position with the target (TARGET_TOLERANCE 0.25 deg, line 53). A refused home sync (request Dec 90 vs real 89.85) is therefore reported by Mount Agent as a successful sync, and the plate solver (indigo_libs/indigo_platesolver.c:743-747) as "Synced"; a refused solve-and-sync near the pole with a larger correction ends "Mount did not reach the target". The mount's own ALERT message does reach clients. The same already applies to the existing "Too many alignment points" refusal. Not caused by this ticket; a follow-up ticket could make Mount Agent remember an ALERT seen after its request.
-

Re-review of tree 16f68f12 against fedf50f0 (my changes verdict). Only 4 files changed since then: test_mount_synscan_simulator.c, test_mount_alignment_load.c, and the SynScan README/TEST_SUMMARY simulator record. indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c and the SynScan driver are unchanged.

Must-fix resolved: indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c:3341 now compares refused_ra with home_ra (tolerance 0.01 h, wrapped). Both values are the published pointing with no alignment points: the raw RA of the home position, which is the J2000 place of the pole of date (23.9885 h / 11.9885 h) and does not depend on LST, and synscan_wrap_hours handles the 0/24 h boundary. The check therefore no longer depends on the sidereal time. Non-adoption of the request is still proven by the declination checks at 3338-3339.

New assertions are correct and not time- or order-dependent: the message and alert flag are cleared before each request (3322-3324, 3372-3375). indigo_change_property is dispatched synchronously (indigo_bus.c:1034) and update_property is delivered before send_message, so the ALERT values and the message are recorded before the request call returns, and nothing races. The Dec 86 check (3380) compares the ALERT declination with the J2000 declination of the GoTo target just reached; the earlier check already requires that pointing to within 0.01 deg, and the drift over a few seconds without tracking is negligible. Unit test (test_mount_alignment_load.c:161-187): RA is set to 1 before the partial request, and the test asserts exactly one refusal, RA unchanged, ALERT and no new point.

Records: the README and TEST_SUMMARY simulator line was replaced by 2026-11-18 22:14 97/97, following the script's replace rule. The AZ-GTi 21:50 20/20 record stays and remains valid because the hardware case and the library are unchanged.

Ran: unit test 3/3 PASS; synscan_mount_refuses_sync_near_the_pole alone PASS (rebuilt from the current sources); test-clean afterwards. Not run

Owner decision (2026-11-18): the implemented approach is rejected. Constraints for this ticket: (1) indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c is not changed; (2) the driver must never rewrite coordinates coming from a client (no in-place change of the incoming property, no substitution of other values before handing a request to the base driver); (3) the bus must never show coordinates other than the ones in the frame the driver declares (J2000), not even transiently; alignment point labels included. The sync wrapper synscan_sync_in_the_frame_of_the_date violates (2) and (3) and must go; these are not cosmetic issues because agents and clients act on the published values. The review started on that tree was stopped before a verdict. The recorded runs of 3.0.0.23 (simulator 99/99, AZ-GTi 20/20) belong to the rejected tree and do not count for the final change. A new design is to be agreed with the owner before any further implementation.

Owner instruction (2026-11-18): discard the change of this ticket and redo it with a stronger model. All seven changed files in the worktree were restored to their master content (driver 3.0.0.22, recorded runs of 2026-11-07 and 2026-10-23); the earlier wip commits stay in the branch history and are not rewritten.

history.previous_description:
Origin: a user who upgraded reported that the SynScan driver points the mount in a completely wrong, opposite direction. The report has no version, log or procedure, so the cause below is the most plausible one found by code reading; it was not reproduced on the simulator yet.

Cause: 3.0.0.22 (commit 8dd1ac0ee, released in 3.0-11) fixed J2000 targets being pointed at their place in 2000 by precessing at the axis boundary, after the framework alignment model. MOUNT_RAW_COORDINATES and the alignment points therefore became J2000. In the home position the axes are at Dec 90 of the date; precessed to J2000 this is always about RA 0h / Dec 89.85 regardless of the hour angle, while up to 3.0.0.21 the raw RA there was LST -/+ 6h. The NEAREST_POINT / SINGLE_POINT model stores raw_ra - ra and adds it to every target (indigo_translated_to_raw_with_lst in indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c), so a sync made in the home position (for example RA = LST - 6h, Dec 90), which gave a zero offset before, now records an arbitrary offset of up to 12 hours and later GoTos go far from their targets. Commit d7f5c4e30 only adds a warning for syncs above 85 degrees and is not in 3.0-11.

Requested change (the smaller variant, driver only):
- Keep MOUNT_RAW_COORDINATES and the raw side of the alignment points in the frame of the date, as up to 3.0.0.21, so they are again a direct image of the axes (raw RA = LST - mechanical hour angle).
- GoTo and sync target path in synscan_radec_to_steps: precess the J2000 target to the date first, then apply indigo_translated_to_raw, then form the hour angle.
- Read-back in synscan_read_mount_coordinates: raw of the date from the encoders, through indigo_raw_to_translated_with_lst, then precess the result to J2000 for MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES; horizontal coordinates are computed from the coordinates of the date.
- Keep the driver's MOUNT_PARK_SET / MOUNT_HOME_SET handlers that take CURRENT from the axis counters; they are needed in both variants.
- Keep the 21' precession fix itself: a J2000 target must still be pointed at its place of the date.
- Increment the driver version in the .driver source and regenerate the checked-in outputs.

Known limitation to state in the ticket result: the framework stores the alignment point's ra from the bus (J2000) and raw_ra from the driver (date), so a point's offset contains the local precession and is off by arcminutes for targets far from the point. Removing that needs a change of indigo_mount_driver.c (store the point's ra precessed to the date) and is out of scope unless the owner approves it separately. Do not change the generator or the mount base driver in this ticket.

Tests (simulator suite indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c):
- new case: sync in the home position to RA = LST -/+ 6h, Dec 90, then a GoTo to a target at moderate declination ends within the usual tolerance of the target, not hours away; the case must fail on 3.0.0.22;
- J2000 GoTo still lands on the place of the date (existing 3.0.0.22 cases adapted to raw coordinates of the date);
- raw coordinates in the home position equal LST -/+ 6h, Dec +/-90, both hemispheres;
- park/home CURRENT and DEFAULT cases remain green.
Final run recorded with python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan; hardware coverage is not part of this ticket and stays a stated gap.

Also update CHANGELOG-relevant behaviour notes only through the normal release process; indigo_docs/PROPERTIES.md needs no change (no property added or removed).
history.description:
Origin: a user who upgraded to 3.0-11 reported that the SynScan driver points the mount in a completely wrong, opposite direction.

Cause (reproduced on the simulator, see the notes): since 3.0.0.22 the driver's coordinates are J2000 throughout (raw coordinates, aligned coordinates, alignment points), which is consistent and stays as it is. In the home position the axes are at Dec 90 of the date, i.e. about RA 0h / Dec 89.85 J2000 whatever the hour angle. A sync is an alignment point of the framework model, which adds raw_ra - ra to every target it is used for. A sync in the home position (for example RA = LST - 6 h, Dec 90, a no-op up to 3.0.0.21) therefore records an arbitrary right ascension offset of hours, and later GoTos end hours of hour angle away (8.25 h in the reproduction). Near the pole the right ascension is ill-defined and no right ascension offset can be measured there at all.

Owner decisions (2026-11-18), binding for this ticket:
- indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c and the generator are not changed.
- The driver never rewrites coordinates coming from a client and never hands other values than the client's to the base driver.
- The bus never shows coordinates other than the real J2000 ones, not even transiently, alignment point labels included.
- The coordinate frames of 3.0.0.22 are kept exactly (no precession moved, raw coordinates stay J2000).
- A sync within 5 degrees of the pole is refused with ALERT and a message.

Requested change (driver only, indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver, regenerated outputs):
- In the sync branch of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES (framework alignment modes, i.e. not CONTROLLER), before the request is handed to indigo_mount_change_property: when the requested declination or the current raw declination is more than 85 degrees from the equator, refuse the sync. MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES ends in ALERT with a message that says why and what to do (sync on a star below 85 degrees of declination); no alignment point is added; the client's values are not adopted, the property keeps publishing the real coordinates of the mount; nothing moves; the next accepted request works normally. Follow the driver's existing refusal pattern (refusal reasons added in 3.0.0.16) and the generated-handler rules in AGENTS.md.
- The limit is 85 degrees, the same as the base driver's pole warning (d7f5c4e30).
- A sync below the limit behaves exactly as in 3.0.0.22.
- Increment the driver version to 23 in the .driver source and regenerate the checked-in outputs with the unchanged generator.

Known limitation to state in the ticket result: alignment points with an offset of hours that 3.0.0.22 already saved from a pole sync stay in the user's configuration until deleted with MOUNT_ALIGNMENT_DELETE_POINTS; the driver cannot tell them from real points.

Tests, simulator suite (indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c), no assertion of an existing case weakened:
- sync in the home position to RA = LST - 6 h / Dec 90 (north) and RA = LST + 6 h / Dec -90 (south): ALERT with the message, alignment point count unchanged, published coordinates still the real ones (not the requested ones) after the next poll, then a GoTo to a target at moderate declination is pointed within the usual tolerance (decode the pointing from the :G/:H commands and the pier side from the DEC axis position); this case must fail on 3.0.0.22;
- sync requested with |Dec| > 85 while the mount stands at moderate declination: refused the same way;
- sync just below the limit and at moderate declination: accepted, alignment point added, exactly as before;
- an existing case that syncs while the mount still stands at the pole (synscan_mount_sync_adds_alignment_point) is moved to a moderate declination first, keeping all its assertions;
- a refused sync leaves the mount usable: following sync below the limit and GoTo succeed.
Hardware suite (indigo_test/hardware/test_mount_synscan_hw.c): the same refusal at the pole and an accepted sync at moderate declination followed by a GoTo, restoring the starting position and deleting its alignment points on every exit path; a case never passes silently when its precondition is not met.

Test runs, both non-interactive and recorded with the script: python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan and python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan --hw against the AZ-GTi on the network (no telescope mounted, it may move as needed; no hot-plug). MIGRATION_STATUS.md test counts updated in the status column only. indigo_docs/PROPERTIES.md needs no change (no property added or removed).

history.previous_description:
Origin: a user who upgraded to 3.0-11 reported that the SynScan driver points the mount in a completely wrong, opposite direction.

Cause (reproduced on the simulator, see the notes): since 3.0.0.22 the driver's coordinates are J2000 throughout (raw coordinates, aligned coordinates, alignment points), which is consistent and stays as it is. In the home position the axes are at Dec 90 of the date, i.e. about RA 0h / Dec 89.85 J2000 whatever the hour angle. A sync is an alignment point of the framework model, which adds raw_ra - ra to every target it is used for. A sync in the home position (for example RA = LST - 6 h, Dec 90, a no-op up to 3.0.0.21) therefore records an arbitrary right ascension offset of hours, and later GoTos end hours of hour angle away (8.25 h in the reproduction). Near the pole the right ascension is ill-defined and no right ascension offset can be measured there at all.

Owner decisions (2026-11-18), binding for this ticket:
- indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c and the generator are not changed.
- The driver never rewrites coordinates coming from a client and never hands other values than the client's to the base driver.
- The bus never shows coordinates other than the real J2000 ones, not even transiently, alignment point labels included.
- The coordinate frames of 3.0.0.22 are kept exactly (no precession moved, raw coordinates stay J2000).
- A sync within 5 degrees of the pole is refused with ALERT and a message.

Requested change (driver only, indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver, regenerated outputs):
- In the sync branch of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES (framework alignment modes, i.e. not CONTROLLER), before the request is handed to indigo_mount_change_property: when the requested declination or the current raw declination is more than 85 degrees from the equator, refuse the sync. MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES ends in ALERT with a message that says why and what to do (sync on a star below 85 degrees of declination); no alignment point is added; the client's values are not adopted, the property keeps publishing the real coordinates of the mount; nothing moves; the next accepted request works normally. Follow the driver's existing refusal pattern (refusal reasons added in 3.0.0.16) and the generated-handler rules in AGENTS.md.
- The limit is 85 degrees, the same as the base driver's pole warning (d7f5c4e30).
- A sync below the limit behaves exactly as in 3.0.0.22.
- Increment the driver version to 23 in the .driver source and regenerate the checked-in outputs with the unchanged generator.

Known limitation to state in the ticket result: alignment points with an offset of hours that 3.0.0.22 already saved from a pole sync stay in the user's configuration until deleted with MOUNT_ALIGNMENT_DELETE_POINTS; the driver cannot tell them from real points.

Tests, simulator suite (indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c), no assertion of an existing case weakened:
- sync in the home position to RA = LST - 6 h / Dec 90 (north) and RA = LST + 6 h / Dec -90 (south): ALERT with the message, alignment point count unchanged, published coordinates still the real ones (not the requested ones) after the next poll, then a GoTo to a target at moderate declination is pointed within the usual tolerance (decode the pointing from the :G/:H commands and the pier side from the DEC axis position); this case must fail on 3.0.0.22;
- sync requested with |Dec| > 85 while the mount stands at moderate declination: refused the same way;
- sync just below the limit and at moderate declination: accepted, alignment point added, exactly as before;
- an existing case that syncs while the mount still stands at the pole (synscan_mount_sync_adds_alignment_point) is moved to a moderate declination first, keeping all its assertions;
- a refused sync leaves the mount usable: following sync below the limit and GoTo succeed.
Hardware suite (indigo_test/hardware/test_mount_synscan_hw.c): the same refusal at the pole and an accepted sync at moderate declination followed by a GoTo, restoring the starting position and deleting its alignment points on every exit path; a case never passes silently when its precondition is not met.

Test runs, both non-interactive and recorded with the script: python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan and python3 tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan --hw against the AZ-GTi on the network (no telescope mounted, it may move as needed; no hot-plug). MIGRATION_STATUS.md test counts updated in the status column only. indigo_docs/PROPERTIES.md needs no change (no property added or removed).
history.description:
Origin: a user who upgraded to 3.0-11 reported that the SynScan driver moves the mount in the opposite direction on GoTo; it was correct before 3.0.0.22.

Cause, established by running the same sequence on an AZ-GTi with drivers 3.0.0.20, 3.0.0.21 and 3.0.0.22 and reading the axis counters straight from the motor controller (see the notes): GoTos without an alignment point end at the same axis positions in all three versions (3.0.0.22 differs by the intended precession only). After a sync in the home position (RA = LST - 6 h, Dec 90) 3.0.0.20 and 3.0.0.21 go where they went without it, 3.0.0.22 ends on the other side of the pier (target HA +2.5 h: RA axis +313314 instead of -302393 steps) and still publishes the target coordinates. Since 3.0.0.22 the raw coordinates are J2000, so at the pole of the date the raw right ascension no longer equals LST - hour angle and the alignment point of the framework model records a right ascension offset of hours. Near the pole no right ascension offset can be measured in any frame.

Owner decision (2026-11-18, supersedes the earlier ones in the notes): change the pole sync warning of indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c (commit d7f5c4e30, not released yet) into a refusal with an error. The SynScan driver itself is not changed; its coordinate frames stay as in 3.0.0.22.

Change:
- indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c, sync branch of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES in the framework alignment modes: when the requested declination or the raw declination is more than 85 degrees from the equator, the request is refused: MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES is published in ALERT with a message, no alignment point is added and the requested values are not adopted, the property keeps the real pointing. The warning message on the BUSY property is removed. A request without the declination item is judged by the declination the property holds.
- Tests: unit case of the warning turned into the refusal (indigo_test/unit/test_mount_alignment_load.c); SynScan simulator suite: new case for the refused home sync in both hemispheres followed by an accurate GoTo, the existing sync case leaves the pole first; mount simulator suite: the case that synced at the pole leaves it first; SynScan hardware suite: new case for the refused home sync followed by an accurate GoTo.
- Recorded runs: tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan (simulator) and --hw (AZ-GTi on the network, non-interactive, no hot-plug).

Known limitation: alignment points with an offset of hours that a pole sync already saved under 3.0.0.22 stay in the user's configuration until deleted with MOUNT_ALIGNMENT_DELETE_POINTS. Baseline: mount_abort_allows_fresh_goto of the mount simulator suite fails on master as well (test_mount_simulator.c, target RA after an alignment mode change) and is not part of this ticket.

Result (2026-11-18): the pole sync warning of indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c is a refusal now: a sync whose requested or raw declination is more than 85 degrees from the equator ends ALERT with 'Sync refused: right ascension is ill-defined within 5 degrees of the celestial pole, sync below 85 degrees of declination', adds no alignment point and does not adopt the requested values. reviews.notes:
Verdict: changes (one must-fix in the new simulator test; the library change itself is correct).

MUST-FIX
1. indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c:3338 - SERIAL_CHECK_TRUE(fabs(synscan_wrap_hours(refused_ra - sync_values[0])) > 1) depends on the sidereal time. In the home position the reported RA is fixed (23.9885 h north / 11.9885 h south, the J2000 place of the pole of date, see the case printout), while the requested RA is LST - 6 h (north) / LST + 6 h (south). Whenever LST is between about 4.99 h and 6.99 h the two are within 1 h in both hemispheres and the case fails although the driver behaves correctly: roughly 2 sidereal hours per day, so the recorded suite is time-of-day flaky. Fix: assert the refusal carried the real pointing instead, e.g. SERIAL_CHECK_TRUE(fabs(synscan_wrap_hours(refused_ra - home_ra)) < 0.01); the declination checks at 3335-3336 already prove the requested values were not adopted. Re-run the case (and the recorded run if the owner wants the record on the final tree).

LIMITATIONS (for the owner, not blocking)
- indigo_drivers/agent_mount/indigo_agent_mount.c:433-495 with indigo_drivers/mount_synscan/indigo_mount_synscan.driver:983-985: the refusal ALERT is transient on SynScan, its next poll republishes MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES OK. A sync is never BUSY, so Mount Agent waits its full 3 s BUSY window, then sees OK and only compares the position with the target (TARGET_TOLERANCE 0.25 deg, line 53). A refused home sync (request Dec 90 vs real 89.85) is therefore reported by Mount Agent as a successful sync, and the plate solver (indigo_libs/indigo_platesolver.c:743-747) as "Synced"; a refused solve-and-sync near the pole with a larger correction ends "Mount did not reach the target". The mount's own ALERT message does reach clients. The same already applies to the existing "Too many alignment points" refusal. Not caused by this ticket; a follow-up ticket could make Mount Agent remember an ALERT seen after its request.
- A near-pole sync sent while a GoTo is BUSY sets the coordinates ALERT mid-slew (base branch has no BUSY guard; the accepted sync already set OK there before). SynScan's poll restores BUSY.
- Alignment points saved earlier near the pole are still loaded (indigo_mount_driver.c:471), as stated in the ticket.
- Only mount_synscan and mount_simulator can reach this branch: MOUNT_ALIGNMENT_MODE is hidden (not defined, not changeable) in every other driver and defaults to CONTROLLER. Their raw declination is maintained; no driver gets a behaviour change that looks wrong.

NITS
- test_mount_synscan_simulator.c:3321: observed_coordinates_message is not cleared per hemisphere, so the second "celestial pole" message check can pass on the first iteration's text; clear it with the alert flag.
- test_mount_synscan_simulator.c:3364-3368: the far (Dec 86) refusal checks ALERT and no point but not the message or that the pointing stayed.
- indigo_test/unit/test_mount_alignment_load.c:162-169: the partial request checks ALERT and the point count but not that RA stayed 1 or that the refusal message was sent.
- indigo_test/hardware/test_mount_synscan_hw.c:996-1001: the refusal is recognised by any message containing "celestial pole", without checking the ALERT state of MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES.

VERIFIED
- Diff master...HEAD: 8 files as listed; the SynScan .driver/.c are identical to master (only README test record changed); nothing from the discarded attempts remains. No other reference to the removed warning (git grep).
- indigo_mount_driver.c:799-818: requested Dec taken from the request, held value when the item is missing; CONTROLLER and too-many-points refusals keep precedence; pole refusal (strictly > 85, requested or raw) happens before indigo_property_copy_values, publishes ALERT with message through indigo_update_coordinates; the property keeps the real pointing.
- Unit test built and run: 3/3 PASS. SynScan case synscan_mount_refuses_sync_near_the_pole run alone (INDIGO_TEST_FILTER): PASS, printout confirms ALERT and next poll carry 23.9885 h/+89.8503 and 11.9885 h/-89.8503, GoTo HA 2.5000 h Dec +30.0000 west.
- Mount simulator suite run twice in the worktree: 28/28 once, once failed at test_mount_simulator.c:606 (mount_abort_allows_fresh_goto, target RA after the alignment mode change). That case syncs in CONTROLLER mode and never reaches the changed branch, so it looks like a pre-existing intermittent failure; I did not run it on master.
- Adapted cases (sync_adds_alignment_point, alignment_model_is_frozen_during_slew) only leave the pole before syncing; no assertion removed or weakened. HW case does all motion first, restores alignment points and position, then asserts; it cannot pass silently. MIGRATION_STATUS.md changes only the counts; README/TEST_SUMMARY lines follow the script's replace rule; PROPERTIES.md needs no change; no doc describes the near-pole sync as accepted or warned.
- Not run by me: full SynScan simulator suite, any hardware test.

Re-review of tree 16f68f12 against fedf50f0 (my changes verdict). Only 4 files changed since then: test_mount_synscan_simulator.c, test_mount_alignment_load.c, and the SynScan README/TEST_SUMMARY simulator record. indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c and the SynScan driver are unchanged.

Must-fix resolved: indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c:3341 now compares refused_ra with home_ra (tolerance 0.01 h, wrapped). Both values are the published pointing with no alignment points: the raw RA of the home position, which is the J2000 place of the pole of date (23.9885 h / 11.9885 h) and does not depend on LST, and synscan_wrap_hours handles the 0/24 h boundary. The check therefore no longer depends on the sidereal time. Non-adoption of the request is still proven by the declination checks at 3338-3339.

New assertions are correct and not time- or order-dependent: the message and alert flag are cleared before each request (3322-3324, 3372-3375). indigo_change_property is dispatched synchronously (indigo_bus.c:1034) and update_property is delivered before send_message, so the ALERT values and the message are recorded before the request call returns, and nothing races. The Dec 86 check (3380) compares the ALERT declination with the J2000 declination of the GoTo target just reached; the earlier check already requires that pointing to within 0.01 deg, and the drift over a few seconds without tracking is negligible. Unit test (test_mount_alignment_load.c:161-187): RA is set to 1 before the partial request, and the test asserts exactly one refusal, RA unchanged, ALERT and no new point.

Records: the README and TEST_SUMMARY simulator line was replaced by 2026-11-18 22:14 97/97, following the script's replace rule. The AZ-GTi 21:50 20/20 record stays and remains valid because the hardware case and the library are unchanged.

Ran: unit test 3/3 PASS; synscan_mount_refuses_sync_near_the_pole alone PASS (rebuilt from the current sources); test-clean afterwards. Not run: the full suites and the hardware tests.

The limitations of the previous review stand (Mount Agent may report a refused sync as success on SynScan because the poll republishes OK; points saved earlier near the pole are still loaded). The hardware nit was deliberately not changed. No must-fix remains.

notes.text: Cause confirmed on the simulator (macOS arm64, 2026-11-18) with a one-off case built outside the repository against the unchanged simulator and suite helpers: latitude 48, no alignment points, sync in the home position to RA = LST - 6 h / Dec 90, then a GoTo to the J2000 place of HA +2.5 h / Dec +30 of the date; the pointing is decoded from the :G/:H commands. Both are non-interactive runs (defects found are fixed and the full scope rerun), recorded with tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan and tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan --hw. This replaces the earlier statement that hardware coverage is not part of this ticket. Physical hot-plug is not part of the run.

Result (implementer, 2026-11-18). Regression case synscan_mount_goto_after_sync_in_home_position (sync RA=LST-6h Dec 90 in home, lat 48, GoTo to J2000 place of HA +2.5h Dec +30): after the fix the axes end at HA 2.5000 h Dec +30.0000 (3.0.0.22: 8.25 h off); pier side decoded from the DEC axis position. Driver 3.0.0.23: raw coordinates are of the date again; GoTo precesses J2000 to date before indigo_translated_to_raw; read-back raw(date) -> indigo_raw_to_translated_with_lst -> precess to J2000, horizontal from the aligned coordinates of the date. Added beyond the brief: syncs from the bus are precessed to the date (synscan_sync_in_the_frame_of_the_date) unless |Dec|>85, otherwise a sync round trip was off by the precession (sync_adds_alignment_point failed with 0.05 h / 0.15 deg) and a GoTo to the synced target landed ~5' off; within 5 deg of the pole the sync is taken as given so a typed home position stays offset-free. Residual limitation: a point's offset still mixes frames only for pole syncs and for targets far from a point arcminute-level; base-driver change out of scope. Scenario mapping (simulator): home sync + GoTo -> synscan_mount_goto_after_sync_in_home_position; raw coordinates in home, LST -/+6h and Dec +/-90 at lat 48 and -35 -> synscan_mount_raw_coordinates_of_the_home_position_follow_the_sidereal_time; GoTo to synced target returns to synced axes -> synscan_mount_goto_to_the_synced_target_returns_to_the_synced_axes; J2000 target at its place of date -> synscan_mount_points_j2000_coordinates_at_their_place_of_date (unchanged assertions); fresh_date_pointing/home/sync/abort/refused/busy/guider cases adapted to raw coordinates of the date (4 cases compared raw Dec with the J2000 target; now compared with its date Dec, same tolerances). Recorded runs: simulator 99/99 OK (2026-11-18 19:36, mac arm64); hardware AZ-GTi (Sky-Watcher SynScan AZGTi, firmware 3.16, synscan://192.168.111.139:11880 via UDP autodetection) 20/20 OK (2026-11-18 20:17) incl. new case synscan_sync_near_the_pole_keeps_goto_accurate: sync at the pole, GoTo reached HA +1.0001 h Dec 60.0000, across the meridian HA -1.0000 h Dec 60.0000, point removed, mount returned. Earlier hw attempts: first failed at connect_device(mount) (UDP autodetection lost the exchange; second attempt succeeded), one hw run failed my new case (wrong sign in the expectation, fixed) - not recorded. Hot-plug not run.

Owner decision (2026-11-18): the implemented approach is rejected. Constraints for this ticket: (1) indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c is not changed; (2) the driver must never rewrite coordinates coming from a client (no in-place change of the incoming property, no substitution of other values before handing a request to the base driver); (3) the bus must never show coordinates other than the ones in the frame the driver declares (J2000), not even transiently; alignment point labels included. The sync wrapper synscan_sync_in_the_frame_of_the_date violates (2) and (3) and must go; these are not cosmetic issues because agents and clients act on the published values. The review started on that tree was stopped before a verdict. The recorded runs of 3.0.0.23 (simulator 99/99, AZ-GTi 20/20) belong to the rejected tree and do not count for the final change. A new design is to be agreed with the owner before any further implementation.

All seven changed files in the worktree were restored to their master content (driver 3.0.0.22, recorded runs of 2026-11-07 and 2026-10-23); the earlier wip commits stay in the branch history and are not rewritten.
